Erfar the Silvertongue

Overview

Erfar the Silvertongue governs Gipath’s village and presents himself as its devoted elected leader. He proclaims Zak the Chosen and puts that supposed destiny to practical use, assigning dangerous errands while promising honour and hospitality. His speeches conceal a much more personal interest in the island. [1, 2]

The village and the Chosen

At the village assembly, Erfar the Silvertongue identifies Zak with the promised Chosen who was to appear at the Sacred Ruins. Gort the Skullcrusher, the captain, supports the ceremony. The offer of food, shelter and honour comes with a threat: an impostor would be thrown into the fire. Zak accepts the title and gives his name. Erfar immediately sends him against the goblin sentry watching the village, reasoning that his plain clothes and unusual metal knife will let him approach where armed villagers cannot. Afterwards Zak learns that this is Gipath’s only human village, with no king or known route to other lands. [2, 1, 3, 4]

The wolf, the captain and the craftsman

Killing the sentry brings another request from Erfar: the White Wolf and its pack are taking the village livestock. After Zak kills their leader, Erfar and Gort press him to surrender the head so the captain can claim prestige. Gort also sends him to punish the goblins while the village soldiers stay home. Meanwhile Babur the Tightfist refuses to work until his stolen iron tools are returned. Erfar calls the thieves friendly “Free Hunters”; Babur calls them brigands and describes the beating of his apprentice. Recovering the chisel and bodkin from the chief and his wife wins Zak the craftsman’s services. These early errands expose the disagreement between the village’s leaders and the man who equips it. [5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12]

Two searches on the islands

The river islands hold two different leads. Estera needs the Orb, which Erfar places on the southernmost island. Erfar also proposes tracing GoGo’s blue Eye Stone to a possible portal. Zak takes the First Goblin’s skull to compel GoGo to visit the village; the chief explains that the orcs confiscated the written record of the stone’s origin. The islands require their own bridge mechanism, distinct from the cave’s. Zak retrieves the record and the Orb in this area. Erfar claims the record offers nothing useful, then diverts attention to missing taxes and gold in Golden Valley. His portal scheme and Estera’s search serve different purposes, even though they take Zak through the same territory. [13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21]

The Orb and the Dead City

When Estera uses the Orb, Zak sees an old man instead of a recognisable memory. She believes he is its owner and a more powerful magician who might help. Orc records trace the object to the Dead City. Estera distinguishes its human fortress from Gipath’s much older ruins: after the Night of Troubles, the dead attacked the living, and survivors fled to found the present village. The obvious route into the fortress is deadly. Airy leaves to investigate another way in, despite her grandmother’s objections. Separately, Erfar can send Zak into the surrounding region’s Golden Valley for a caravan’s lost treasure, an errand he badly understates. [22, 23, 24, 16, 25, 26, 27]

The supposed attack on the goblins

While Zak seeks the magician, Erfar and Gort arrange another joint operation with the Free Hunters, supposedly to prevent a goblin raid. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility, while Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. [28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34]

Gort’s rebellion

The written instructions to kill Zak expose Gort’s handwriting. Confronted with the evidence, the captain turns against the authority he formerly served and declares that he will rule the village himself. He flees to gather the forest men. Erfar urges Zak to stop him before he can return; the ensuing pursuit ends Gort’s rebellion. Rivar the Hulk becomes the new captain. Unlike his predecessor, Rivar admits that he dislikes fighting, shares his family’s secret of strength and later supports Zak when suspicion finally reaches the elder. [35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42]

The White Flower and Erfar’s exposure

After Gort’s fall, Erfar claims that an orc seer has cursed the village with disease and asks for a White Flower. Zak finds armed opposition waiting for him, although no villagers have yet fallen ill. Erfar blames Babur, while Babur’s earlier warning makes Zak suspect both men. Estera suggests setting a trap. Zak tells each suspect a different location for a second flower; the ambush appears at the place he gave Erfar. With Rivar’s support he confronts and imprisons the elder. An expedition report recovered from the abandoned foreign camp becomes leverage: Erfar translates its account of a concealed tunnel and its opening lever. He later escapes custody. Estera recalls that he originally arrived as an adult stranger, leaving his real purpose unresolved. [43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 40, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52]

Brother Faceless and the return to Gipath

Khatul asks Brother Faceless to help Zak reach the guarded portal. Faceless arranges a cave meeting and explains the keys and stone controls. He then reveals himself as Erfar: born on Suslanger, he went to Gipath seeking the meteorite and manipulated the villagers into searching for it. His earlier plots were attempts to remove Zak, who disrupted that scheme. The reunion is another trap, with guards waiting outside the cave. Zak survives the confrontation and forces a route through the portal’s defences. Activating its two controls finally returns him to Tka-Rik with the amulet fragments. [53, 54, 55, 56, 57]
